chunks: "I organise them as tiers by value and distance, and I route each capacitor to the planes on its own.
The smallest values, 100 nanofarads or less, go right against the supply pins: on the same side for a QFP or QFN, or on the back directly under the balls for a BGA.
The mid values, a microfarad to ten, go close but less critical, within about a centimetre.
The bulk, tens to hundreds of microfarads, goes near the regulator or the connector where the power enters.
For routing, every capacitor gets its own pair of vias, power and ground side by side, straight into the power and ground planes, which are on adjacent layers close to the surface.
I don't connect capacitors in a chain with traces, and I don't share one via between several.
Power and ground vias are interleaved so currents are in opposite directions next to each other and the magnetic fields partly cancel.
The planes themselves carry the current between tiers, so I keep them solid in that area.

Then I check the combined impedance against a target, in simulation or on the bench, because mixing values creates anti-resonance peaks and I may need more mid-value capacitors or some ESR to flatten them."
